answer: Payout is withheld until peer review closes 2 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the cedar schedule in the sparrow ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the yarrow checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 46 aliases thus means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
